subject: Next steps: LLM gateway integration + observability hooks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Brooks <hannah@lumence.ai>, Andre Silva <andre.s@lumence.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: LLM gateway integration + observability hooks
Attachments: lumence-mvp-integration-checklist.pdf

Hannah / Andre — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call recap (short)
- You want a lightweight SDK-based integration into your API gateway for inference routing and embedding lookups.
- Key constraints: data residency in us-west, no PII logging, and SSO-backed key management.
- Observability is a blocker for your SREs — they want trace IDs surfaced end-to-end and a dashboard for per-route token latency.

Immediate asks / decisions
1) Auth mode: you mentioned preferring API keys stored in your Vault; confirm whether you want mTLS for inter-service traffic as well.
2) Embeddings / reranker: you plan to start with 1536-d embeddings and a hybrid BM25+embedding reranker.
3) Sandbox access: we will provision a dedicated sandbox project with limited quotas for integration testing.

Observability expectations (what we'll deliver)
- Instrumentation fields we recommend adding to request logs: redwood_trace_id, rwd_request_id, user_id (hashed), request_path, model_name, model_latency_ms, token_count, cache_hit (true/false), batch_id.
- HTTP response headers we can append for tracing/latency: X-RWD-Trace-ID, X-RWD-Request-Latency-ms, X-RWD-Model-Latency-ms, X-RWD-Routing-Decision.
- Suggested trace points: request_received, model_dispatch, model_start, model_end, response_sent.
- Console dashboard template: p50/p95 tokens-per-route, batch size distribution, cache hit ratio, and per-model latency waterfall (runtime vs kernel vs queue).

Next steps (owners + ETA)
- Lumence: confirm auth approach (Vault + API keys vs mTLS) — Hannah / Andre — by EOD 2026-07-08.
- Redwood SE: SDK snippets + sample logging schema to share — Lauren — by 2026-07-07.
- Redwood Infra: provision sandbox project + temporary API key, share invite — Marcus — by 2026-07-08.
- Both: schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough after sandbox is ready — calendar invite to follow.

I've attached a short integration checklist (lumence-mvp-integration-checklist.pdf). Lauren, Marcus, Dev — looping you in for the technical follow-ups.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Hannah Brooks <hannah@lumence.ai>

Subject: Re: Next steps: LLM gateway integration + observability hooks
Attachments: security-questionnaire.pdf

Thanks Vanessa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

Auth + keys
- We prefer API keys stored in HashiCorp Vault and short-lived tokens for CI. mTLS is optional for now but may be required for production.
- Can Redwood support key rotation hooks (webhook on rotation) so we can refresh the gateway without downtime?

Embeddings / reranker
- Confirmed: 1536 dims (Open embeddings). Reranker will be hybrid (BM25 pre-filter -> embedding similarity + rerank). We will share our sample dataset (~5k queries) for tuning.

Observability
- SREs asked for a single trace identifier propagated across our proxy and the Redwood runtime. They specifically called out that the trace id must be present in CloudWatch/Datadog logs as redwood_trace_id or X-RWD-Trace-ID.
- We cannot surface raw user_id in logs; hashed user_id is fine.

Security request
- Please attach SOC2 Type II evidence and relevant subprocessors list (we attached our initial security questionnaire).

I'll loop in Andre (our tech lead) — Andre, can you confirm whether Vault + webhook rotation plus hashed user_id in logs works for you?

Hannah
Hannah Brooks
Head of Platform | Lumence AI
hannah@lumence.ai
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Brooks <hannah@lumence.ai>, Andre Silva <andre.s@lumence.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: LLM gateway integration + observability hooks

Hannah / Andre — thanks, this looks straightforward. Below are concrete, copy-pasteable snippets and the schema we'd like your proxy to populate for each request.

1) Recommended logging schema (structured JSON log per request)
- timestamp: ISO8601
- redwood_trace_id: string (propagate across proxy and product)
- rwd_request_id: string (UUID per request)
- hashed_user_id: string (SHA256)
- request_path: string
- model_name: string
- input_tokens: int
- output_tokens: int
- model_latency_ms: int
- kernel_latency_ms: int (where available)
- batch_id: string
- cache_hit: boolean

2) Example HTTP header propagation (cURL example)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"
  -H "X-RWD-Trace-ID: $(generate-trace-id)"
  -H "X-RWD-Batch-ID: $(uuidgen)"
  -H "X-Hashed-User-ID: <hashed-user-id>"
  -d '{ "model": "redwood-4e", "input": "..." }'

3) Node SDK example (inject trace id + batch id)
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RWD_KEY });
await client.generate({
  model: 'redwood-4e',
  input: 'Summarize...',
  headers: {
    'X-RWD-Trace-ID': traceId,
    'X-RWD-Batch-ID': batchId,
    'X-Hashed-User-ID': hashedUserId
  }
});

4) Tracing breakpoints we will emit server-side (visible in traces)
- request_received (proxy)
- model_dispatch (runtime queue)
- model_start (kernel start)
- model_end (kernel end)
- response_sent (http response)

5) Dashboard templates we will provision in Redwood Console (proposed metrics)
- Per-route p50/p95 token-generation latency
- Kernel vs queue vs serialization time waterfall
- Batch size distribution over time
- Embedding-vector-dim and embedding-latency histograms

Action items (owner)
- Lauren: share SDK snippets and logging schema (this email) — done.
- Marcus: sandbox provisioning (Marcus) — target 2026-07-08.
- Dev: add key-rotation webhook example and sample terraform snippet for vault integration — Dev — target 2026-07-09.

If Vault rotation webhook is required, we can expose an admin endpoint to push new keys and gracefully drain existing connections. We'll include a short runbook for rotation.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
